param.label: BAM files
param.help: List of indexed BAM files. The dataset name (without .bam) is used as the sample label, so cells are reported as label::barcode. Identical names get a numeric suffix (_2, _3, ...).

param.label: BAM file
param.help: Indexed BAM file.

macros.token: #import re #set $bam_args = [] #set $label_args = [] #set $seen_labels = set() #for $i, $bam in enumerate($bamfiles) #set $base_label = re.sub(r'[^\w\-.]', '_', re.sub(r'\.bam$', '', str($bam.element_identifier))) #set $label = $base_label #set $n = 2 #while $label in $seen_labels #set $label = '%s_%d' % ($base_label, $n) #set $n += 1 #end while #silent $seen_labels.add($label) ln -s '$bam' 'input_${i}.bam' && ln -s '${bam.metadata.bam_index}' 'input_${i}.bam.bai' && #silent $bam_args.append("'input_%s.bam'" % $i) #silent $label_args.append("'%s'" % $label) #end for

param.label: Barcodes
param.help: A single-column file containing the cell barcode whitelist, one barcode per line.

param.label: Cell tag
param.help: Name of the BAM tag from which to extract barcodes.

validator.message: A BAM tag consists of two alphanumeric characters

param.label: @LABEL@
param.help: sincei-generated input file in .h5ad (AnnData) format.

param.label: Region
param.help: Region of the genome to limit the operation to - this is useful when testing parameters to reduce the computing time. The format is chr:start:end (chr:start-end is also accepted), for example chr10 or chr10:456700:891000.

validator.message: Use the format chr, chr:start:end or chr:start-end

param.label: Bin size
param.help: Size of the bins, in bases, to calculate coverage.

param.label: Distance between bins
param.help: The gap length, in bases, between bins for calculating coverage. Larger values can be used to sample the genome for input files with high coverage while smaller values are useful for lower coverage data. Note that if you specify a value that results in too few (<1000) reads sampled, the value will be decreased.

param.label: Blacklist
param.help: A BED or GTF file containing regions that should be excluded from all analyses. Currently this works by rejecting genomic chunks that happen to overlap an entry. Consequently, for BAM files, if a read partially overlaps a blacklisted region or a fragment spans over it, then the read/fragment might still be considered.

param.label: Chromosomes to skip
param.help: List of chromosome names to skip from the analysis. Regions on these chromosomes will be excluded. Useful for skipping mitochondrial, X chromosome, or unplaced contigs. Separate multiple chromosomes with commas, e.g. chrM,chrX.

macros.token: #if $exclusion.blacklist: --blacklist #for $bl in $exclusion.blacklist '$bl' #end for #end if #if str($exclusion.chrToSkip).strip(): --chrToSkip #for $chrom in str($exclusion.chrToSkip).split(',') #if $chrom.strip() '${chrom.strip()}' #end if #end for #end if

param.label: Minimum mapping quality
param.help: If set, only reads that have a mapping quality score of at least this are considered.

param.label: SAM flag include
param.help: Include reads based on SAM flag. For example, to get only reads that are the first mate, use a flag of 64. This is useful to count properly paired reads only once, as otherwise the second mate will be also considered for the coverage.

param.label: SAM flag exclude
param.help: Exclude reads based on the SAM flag. For example, to get only reads that map to the forward strand, use 16, where 16 is the SAM flag for reads that map to the reverse strand.

param.label: Duplicate filter
param.help: How to filter for duplicates? Different combinations (using start/end/umi) are possible. Read start position and read barcode are always considered. Leave empty to consider all reads as passing the filter. Note that in case of paired end data, both reads in the fragment are considered (and kept). So if you wish to keep only read1, combine this option with the SAM flag include filter.

macros.token: #if str($filtering.minMappingQuality) not in ('', 'None'): --minMappingQuality $filtering.minMappingQuality #end if #if str($filtering.samFlagInclude) not in ('', 'None'): --samFlagInclude $filtering.samFlagInclude #end if #if str($filtering.samFlagExclude) not in ('', 'None'): --samFlagExclude $filtering.samFlagExclude #end if #if $filtering.duplicateFilter: --duplicateFilter '$filtering.duplicateFilter' #end if

param.label: Minimum fragment length
param.help: The minimum fragment length needed for read/pair inclusion. This option is useful in ATAC-seq experiments, for filtering mono- or di-nucleosome fragments.

param.label: Maximum fragment length
param.help: The maximum fragment length accepted for read/pair inclusion.

macros.token: #if str($filtering.minFragmentLength) not in ('', 'None'): --minFragmentLength $filtering.minFragmentLength #end if #if str($filtering.maxFragmentLength) not in ('', 'None'): --maxFragmentLength $filtering.maxFragmentLength #end if

param.label: Motif filter
param.help: Check whether a given motif is present in the read and the corresponding reference genome. This option checks for the motif at the 5' end of the read and at the 5' overhang in the genome, which is useful in identifying reads properly cut by a restriction enzyme or MNase. For example, to search for an A at the 5' end of the read and TA at the 5' overhang, use A,TA. Reads not containing the given motif are filtered out. Separate multiple motif pairs with spaces.

validator.message: Motifs must contain only A, C, G, T or N, as 'read,genome' pairs separated by spaces

param.label: Genome (2bit)
param.help: If a motif filter is provided, please also provide the genome sequence in 2bit format.

param.label: GC content filter
param.help: Check whether the GC content of the read falls within the provided range. Input format must be 'low,high', where low is the lower bound and high is the upper bound in the fraction of GC (e.g. 0.1,0.9). If the GC content of the reads falls outside the range, they are filtered out.

param.label: Minimum aligned fraction
param.help: Minimum fraction of the reads which should be aligned to be counted. This includes mismatches tolerated by the aligners, but excludes InDels/Clippings.

macros.token: #if str($filtering.motifFilter).strip(): --motifFilter #for $motif in str($filtering.motifFilter).split() '$motif' #end for #end if #if $filtering.genome2bit: --genome2bit '$filtering.genome2bit' #end if #if str($filtering.GCcontentFilter).strip(): --GCcontentFilter '$filtering.GCcontentFilter' #end if #if str($filtering.minAlignedFraction) not in ('', 'None'): --minAlignedFraction $filtering.minAlignedFraction #end if

param.label: Filter RNA strand
param.help: Selects RNA-seq reads (single-end or paired-end) originating from genes on the given strand. This option assumes a standard dUTP-based library preparation (that is, forward keeps minus-strand reads, which originally came from genes on the forward strand using a dUTP-based method). Consider using the SAM flag exclude filter instead for filtering by strand in other contexts.

param.label: Extend reads
param.help: This parameter allows the extension of reads to fragment size. If set, each read is extended, without exception. NOTE: This feature is generally NOT recommended for spliced-read data, such as RNA-seq, as it would extend reads over skipped regions. Single-end: requires a user specified value for the final fragment length. Reads that already exceed this fragment length will not be extended. Paired-end: reads with mates are always extended to match the fragment size defined by the two read mates. Unmated reads, mate reads that map too far apart (>4x fragment length) or even map to different chromosomes are treated like single-end reads.

param.label: Center reads
param.help: By adding this option, reads are centered with respect to the fragment length. For paired-end data, the read is centered at the fragment length defined by the two ends of the fragment. For single-end data, the given fragment length is used. This option is useful to get sharper signal around enriched regions.

**About sincei**
sincei is a toolkit for the exploration of single-cell (epi)genomics data, from BAM files to count matrices, clustering and pseudo-bulk signal. For full documentation, see https://sincei.readthedocs.io
